subject: general
question: Which of the following is a classical Dravidian language?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dravidian languages are a family of around 70 languages spoken primarily in South Asia.
 
• These languages are divided into 4 main groups:
 
 
• South
 
• South-Central
 
• Central
 
• North
 
 
 
• These groups are further divided into 24 sub-groups.
 
• The four major and classical Dravidian languages are:
 
 
• Telugu
 
• Tamil
 
• Malayalam
 
• Kannada
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Classical Languages: 

 
• A classical language is a language with an independent literary tradition and a large and ancient body of written literature.
 
• Classical languages are typically dead languages or show a high degree of diglossia, as the spoken varieties of the language diverge further away from the classical written language over time.
 
• Six languages in India namely Tamil, Telugu, Sanskrit, Kannada, Malayalam, and Odia have been given the status of classical languages.
 
• The first language to be accorded that status is Tamil. Tamil was declared the classical language back in 2004.
 
• As per Schedule VIII of the Constitution of India, 22 languages have been recognized as Scheduled languages.
